notes: Configuration for build.py. Paths are relative to the repository root unless they start with /.

Gallery order is not set here. Desktop stores take their image order from the 'Desktop' table of the review file (the backticked frame numbers in the Images column, up to the first ';'), mobile stores take their slide order from the 'Mobile' table, keyed by the backticked store-set id. Frame numbers are resolved to files through captures/desktop/selection.json (and the captures folder for the side-by-side alternative); mobile roles are resolved to rendered files through each render manifest.
review_row names the row of the review table a store follows (matched on the text before any parenthesis in the first column). A row reading 'As <other store>' copies that store's list.

Rules: every limit below comes from analysis/mobile-store-comparables.md (observed 2026-11-24) or the storefront-v1 packaging records, unless the 'unverified' list of the store says otherwise. build.py fails on any breach.
switch: the platforms.json platform whose ai_coplay switch must be on for an ai_coplay image to be packaged; a review row that puts co-play on a store whose switch is off is an error.

trailer: per store, the trailer slots, following the 'Which file goes to which store' table of trailer.review. Each file is looked up in trailer.dir (committed: WebM, posters) or trailer.outside_dir (the MP4s, not committed), checked against its bytes, SHA-256 and ffprobe facts in trailer.manifest, and linked (symbolic link) into the package's trailer/ folder. coplay: true means the cut shows AI co-play, so the store's ai_coplay switch must be on. hosted: the store takes a video URL (YouTube, Vimeo) rather than a file, so the slot is reported as blocked, 'needs a hosted video URL', with the file to upload there linked. repo_url: the slot uses the file's raw.githubusercontent.com URL.

copyright: the product copyright line the owner decided on 2026-11-25 (planning/storefront-rollout.md, decision 11). The top-level block holds the line and its variants: line (with ©), plain (where © is unavailable or the platform adds it) and apple (Apple prints its own leading ©). Each store's copyright entry gives the exact value to enter, the field and when; value null means the store has no copyright field to fill. build.py does not read these entries.

appstream.title: AppStream / Flathub (game repository metainfo)

copyright.when: None: AppStream metainfo has no copyright element (the licence is project_license; developer name unchanged).

trailer.note: The master as VP9 in WebM, the form the AppStream spec asks for (VP9 or AV1 in WebM or Matroska). Committed in the repository so its URL is stable; screenshots.xml gets it as a last, non-default screenshot (the spec forbids a video as the default screenshot).

unverified: Whether Flathub or a given software centre plays the AppStream video is not verified (trailer review, store table).

Flathub's current screenshot guidance (size, count, caption length) was not re-read for v2; 1920x1080 PNG follows the brief. The image URLs only resolve after the Git steward commits the PNGs at the listed repository paths (run build.py --stage-appstream to copy them there) and pushes to main.
